analysis.investment_thesis: Anupam Rasayan is a specialty chemicals company with structural China+1 tailwinds and a good promoter holding, but the numbers are deeply troubling: ROE of only 3.32% at a P/E of 85x makes this one of the most expensive-yet-inefficient businesses I've seen in the sector. Revenue has stagnated between INR 1,437–1,602 Cr for three consecutive years while finance costs have nearly doubled.
key_strengths: Promoter holding at 59.1% indicates meaningful skin-in-the-game with a 40-year operating history in specialty chemicals
Long-term contract model with global agrochemical and pharma MNCs provides some revenue visibility
Capital expansion underway (INR 716 Cr capex in FY2024) could unlock revenue growth when new capacities ramp up
key_risks: ROE of 3.32% is catastrophic — the company is destroying shareholder value on a capital-employed basis while trading at 85x earnings
Revenue peaked at INR 1,602 Cr in FY2023 and has contracted for two consecutive years — the growth story has stalled
Finance costs have surged from INR 24 Cr (2019) to INR 112 Cr (2025), rising 4.7x, squeezing net profit margins severely
red_flags: P/E of 85x with ROE of 3.32% is an extreme mismatch — this valuation is completely disconnected from business reality
FCF has been negative in 4 of the last 5 years, including -INR 440 Cr in FY2025, meaning the company is a consistent cash consumer
Net profit has declined from INR 217 Cr (FY2023) to INR 160 Cr (FY2025) — a 26% fall while the stock commands a premium multiple
analysis.detailed_analysis:
I believe in India's specialty chemicals sector as a multi-decade story — the China+1 shift is real and Indian companies should benefit. But a business must earn a decent return on the capital it deploys. An ROE of 3.32% means that for every INR 100 of shareholder equity, this company earns just INR 3.32 — worse than a fixed deposit. Paying 85x earnings for this performance is irrational.

The heavy capex cycle (INR 716 Cr in FY2024 alone) has ballooned the asset base from INR 1,664 Cr to INR 5,650 Cr while profits have actually declined. This is a classic trap where capital keeps entering the business without commensurate returns. Until ROE crosses 15%, revenues return to growth, and valuation compresses to 25-30x, this is a name to avoid entirely. There are far better specialty chemicals plays in India at much more reasonable prices.
